strategies.name: A roadmap for modern digital government 2025 to 2030
A blueprint for modern digital government
Strategic roadmap for public sector data (in development by the Office of the Chief Data Officer; announced for April 2026 and not found published on GOV.UK on 5 November 2026)

decisions.why: Working in the open lets users see and shape priorities; modelled on the data.gov.uk roadmap.

decisions.decision: A hosted chatbot is out of scope
decisions.why: No server, nothing sent anywhere; open data and the MCP server serve approved assistants instead.

decisions.decision: Round 1 waits until Round 0 has recruited for every role
decisions.why: Usability sessions need 5 to 8 people per role, including disabled people.

decisions.decision: Accessibility sessions wait until Round 0 has recruited assistive technology users
decisions.why: The score says Now, but sessions cannot start without participants; the sign-up form (BL-12) and recruitment (BL-13) come first.

decisions.decision: Asking questions in your own words stays in Later
decisions.why: The score says Next, but it needs a way to answer without a server or sending anything anywhere; the open data and MCP server already let approved assistants do this.

decisions.decision: Agreed metadata terms stay in Later
decisions.why: The score says Next, but the terms are for the metadata standards owner to agree, not this portal; the proposed crosswalk stays on the cataloguing page meanwhile.

decisions.decision: Asking questions built without a server
decisions.why: Answers come from the portal's own search index in the reader's browser; nothing is sent anywhere, so the earlier feasibility concern is met.

decisions.decision: Offline copy built as a download of the whole site
decisions.why: A single file would need every page inlined; a zip of the built site opens offline in any browser and stays in step with each release.

items.title: Private feedback route
items.story: As someone without a GitHub account, I need a private way to give feedback, so that I can take part without publishing my views.

items.title: Share
items.story: As a first-time visitor, I need to see how the portal fits together, so that I can find my way without help.

items.title: Signposts to the sister portals
items.story: As a practitioner, I need to know when another portal goes deeper, so that I do not miss tools or evidence.

items.title: Estate compass
items.story: As someone working across policy, practice and technology, I need to know where to start and in what order, so that I take the shortest route to a result.

items.title: Research
items.story: As a user, I need to see what is planned and how decisions are made, and to suggest and vote for ideas, so that the portal meets real needs.

items.title: Round 1: can each role find and follow its steps?
items.story: As the service owner, I need evidence from 5 to 8 people per role, so that changes rest on what users do, not what we assume.

items.title: Test with disabled people and assistive technology
items.story: As someone who uses a screen reader, magnifier or voice control, I need the portal to work with my set-up, so that I can follow the policy like anyone else.

items.title: Private research sign-up form
items.story: As a prospective participant, I need to sign up privately, so that my contact details are not published.

items.title: Round 0: introduce the portal and recruit participants
items.story: As the service owner, I need a pool of participants from every role, organisation type and nation, so that research rounds can start quickly.

items.title: Expert review of the sector supplements
items.story: As a sector specialist, I need the supplements checked by people who know the sector, so that I can trust them.

items.title: Check this flag
items.story: As a policy coordinator, I need to tell you when a capability flag looks wrong, so that the capability model stays accurate.

items.title: Embed a step or table on an intranet
items.story: As a department's data team, I need to show one policy step or table on our intranet, so that colleagues see it where they work.
items.source: Comparison with the Data Quality Commons

items.title: Level labels and easy read summaries
items.story: As someone new to data management, I need to know which pages are pitched at me and to read short plain summaries, so that I am not put off.
items.source: Comparison with the Data Quality Commons

items.title: Ask questions answered from the portal
items.story: As a busy reader, I need to ask a question in my own words and get the page that answers it, so that I do not have to know where things are.
items.source: Comparison with the Data Quality Commons and the catalogue

items.title: Releases feed
items.story: As a returning user, I need to know when something changes, so that I keep up without checking the site.
items.source: Comparison with the Data Quality Commons

items.title: Lineage and ontology downloads
items.story: As a metadata specialist, I need the requirement-to-check lineage and the ontology in open formats, so that I can reuse them in our tools.

items.title: Offline copy
items.story: As someone whose network blocks GitHub Pages, I need a copy I can open offline, so that I can still use the guidance.

items.title: Clearance and an official home
items.story: As a department, I need to know whether this is guidance I can rely on, so that I can use it in my organisation.

items.title: Agreed metadata terms for the four missing properties
items.story: As a catalogue manager, I need agreed terms for every required property, so that our records match everyone else's.

items.title: Welsh language needs
items.story: As someone in a Welsh public body, I may need the portal in Welsh, so that we can meet our language duties.

items.title: Boards, councils and networks
items.story: As a data leader, I need to know which boards decide, which advise and where practitioners meet, so that I can take issues to the right place.

items.title: Get involved and champions toolkit
items.story: As a champion in my organisation, I need ready-made posts, emails and a walk-through, so that I can bring my team in without extra work.

items.title: Badges for taking part
items.story: As someone who helps improve the portal, I want a badge for my profile and signature, so that my contribution is recognised.

items.title: Welsh language summaries
items.story: As someone in a Welsh public body, I need key pages summarised in Welsh, so that we can meet our language duties.

items.title: A chatbot hosted by this portal
items.story: As a reader, I would like to chat with the guidance.
items.reason: Out of scope: the portal runs no server and sends nothing anywhere. Assistants your organisation approves can use its open data and MCP server instead (Use and reuse).
